색.e: Add -색 to make color words: 빨간색 = red.

주인공.m: main character, protagonist; star (of an event)
주인공.x: The main character of this drama is an ordinary office worker.
주인공.t: Also used for the person of honor: 오늘의 주인공 means 'today's star,' like the birthday person.

상반기.ex: 올해 상반기에 새 제품이 나올 예정입니다.
상반기.x: A new product is scheduled to come out in the first half of this year.
상반기.e: Literally 'upper half period' — January to June.

생계.ex: 그는 생계를 위해 두 가지 일을 해요.
생계.x: He works two jobs to make a living.
생계.t: Collocations: 생계를 꾸리다 or 생계를 유지하다 'to make a living'.

공연하다.m: to perform, to put on a show
공연하다.ex: 그 가수는 다음 달에 서울에서 공연할 거예요.
공연하다.x: That singer will perform in Seoul next month.

향하다.m: to head for, go toward; to face
향하다.x: We headed for Busan early in the morning.
향하다.e: From a syllable meaning 'direction, toward', as in 방향 'direction'.
향하다.t: N을/를 향해 means 'toward N': 꿈을 향해 'toward one's dream'.

중시하다.x: Our company values teamwork above all else.
중시하다.t: A formal, written word; in conversation people often say 중요하게 생각하다.

헉.m: gasp!, yikes, oh no (sudden surprise or shock)
헉.x: Yikes, I left my wallet at home!
헉.e: A sound word imitating a sharp intake of breath. Doubled, 헉헉 imitates panting.
헉.t: Casual and very common in texts. 헉 is a quick startled reaction; 헐 is more stunned disbelief.

그렇다고.forms: A. 그렇다고 B. (B usually negative) · fuller form: 그렇다고 해서
그렇다고.m: but that doesn't mean, even so
그렇다고.ex: 일이 많긴 해요. 그렇다고 그만둘 수는 없잖아요.
그렇다고.x: I do have a lot of work. But that doesn't mean I can quit, right?
그렇다고.e: 그렇다 'to be so' + -다고 (quoting): 'just because it is so …'.
그렇다고.t: Pronounced [그러타고]. The next sentence denies the conclusion you might expect: 그렇다고 포기하면 안 돼요 'But that's no reason to give up.'

공과금.m: utility bills, public charges (taxes and fees)
공과금.x: I pay my utility bills automatically every month.
공과금.e: Literally 'public levy money' — electricity, water, gas bills and similar charges.

확진자.ex: 오늘 확진자가 백 명 넘게 나왔습니다.
확진자.x: More than 100 confirmed cases were reported today.
확진자.e: Literally 'person with a certain diagnosis'. -자 = person: 환자, 운전자.
확진자.t: An everyday word since COVID-19; the news says 확진자가 나오다 or 확진자가 발생하다.

현미경.ex: 현미경으로 보니까 작은 세포가 잘 보였어요.
현미경.x: Under the microscope, the tiny cells were clearly visible.

재사용.x: Glass bottles can be washed and reused.
재사용.e: 재- = again, re-: 재사용, 재활용, 재시험.
재사용.t: 재사용 means using the same item again; 재활용 means turning it into something new.

성취감.ex: 마라톤을 끝까지 뛰고 나니 큰 성취감을 느꼈어요.
성취감.x: After running the whole marathon, I felt a great sense of accomplishment.
성취감.t: 보람 is close but focuses on the work feeling worthwhile; 성취감 focuses on reaching a goal.

착실하다.ex: 그 학생은 착실해서 숙제를 한 번도 빠뜨리지 않아요.
착실하다.x: That student is so diligent that she has never missed a homework assignment.
착실하다.e: Literally 'firmly attached to what's real'—solid and dependable.
착실하다.t: Not related to native 착하다 'kind'; 착실하다 means steady and dependable, not nice.

역지사지.m: putting yourself in someone else's shoes
역지사지.x: Before you fight, try putting yourself in their shoes.
역지사지.e: Literally 'swap places and think about it'.

입을 모으다.forms: 입을 모아요 · 입을 모았어요 · 입을 모아 말하다
입을 모으다.m: to say with one voice, to agree unanimously
입을 모으다.ex: 전문가들은 입을 모아 운동의 중요성을 강조했습니다.
입을 모으다.x: Experts unanimously stressed the importance of exercise.
입을 모으다.e: Literally 'to gather mouths' so everyone says the same thing.

평.m: pyeong (unit of area, about 3.3 m² or 35.6 sq ft)
평.e: Traditional unit of about 3.3 square meters, roughly two tatami mats.
평.t: Listings must officially use 제곱미터 (m²), but people still talk about homes in 평.

청문회.ex: 국회는 장관 후보자의 인사 청문회를 열었습니다.
청문회.x: The National Assembly held a confirmation hearing for the minister nominee.
청문회.t: 인사 청문회 is the confirmation hearing for high-level nominees.

경매.ex: 그 그림은 경매에서 십억 원에 팔렸습니다.
경매.x: That painting sold for one billion won at auction.
경매.t: 경매에 나오다 = to come up for auction; 경매에 부치다 = to put up for auction.

선진국.ex: 한국은 짧은 기간에 선진국 대열에 들어섰습니다.
선진국.x: Korea joined the ranks of developed countries in a short time.
선진국.t: 후진국 sounds blunt or insulting today; 개발도상국 is the polite term.

억눌리다.m: to be suppressed, to be oppressed, to be held down
억눌리다.ex: 그동안 억눌렸던 감정이 한꺼번에 터져 나왔어요.
억눌리다.x: All the feelings I'd held down came bursting out at once.
억눌리다.e: Passive of 억누르다 'to suppress', built on 누르다 'to press'.

사뭇.ex: 사진으로 볼 때와 실제 분위기는 사뭇 달랐어요.
사뭇.x: The real atmosphere was strikingly different from the photos.
사뭇.t: Most often heard in 사뭇 다르다 'strikingly different'.

수수방관.m: standing by idly, looking on with folded arms
수수방관.ex: 문제가 커지는데도 정부는 수수방관만 하고 있어요.
수수방관.x: Even as the problem grows, the government is just standing by.
수수방관.e: Literally 'hands in sleeves, watching from the side'.
수수방관.t: Critical tone: used when someone should act but doesn't.

자수성가.m: self-made success; making it on one's own
자수성가.ex: 그분은 가난한 집에서 태어나 자수성가한 사업가예요.
자수성가.x: He's a self-made businessman who was born into a poor family.
자수성가.e: Literally 'building a household with one's own hands.'

국면.ex: 두 나라의 협상이 새로운 국면에 접어들었습니다.
국면.x: The negotiations between the two countries have entered a new phase.
국면.e: Literally 'board surface' — originally the state of a game of baduk, now any situation.
국면.t: Pronounced [궁면] — nasalization; collocations: 국면에 접어들다, 국면을 맞다, 국면 전환.

역효과.m: the opposite effect, backfire, counterproductive result
역효과.ex: 너무 심하게 꾸짖으면 오히려 역효과가 날 수 있어요.
역효과.x: Scolding too harshly can actually backfire.

통로.ex: 비상시에는 통로에 짐을 두면 안 됩니다.
통로.x: In an emergency, you must not leave bags in the aisle.
통로.t: Pronounced [통노] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

자제력.ex: 화가 나도 자제력을 잃지 않도록 노력해요.
자제력.x: Even when I'm angry, I try not to lose my self-control.

학원가.m: private academy district, cram school area
학원가.x: The Daechi-dong academy district is crowded with students until late at night.

강연회.x: Yesterday I went to a lecture by a famous writer.

공천.ex: 그는 당의 공천을 받아 국회의원 선거에 출마했어요.
공천.x: He got his party's nomination and ran for the National Assembly.
공천.t: Common phrases: 공천을 받다 (get the nomination) and 공천에서 탈락하다 (be passed over).

국수주의.ex: 지나친 국수주의는 다른 문화를 배척하게 만듭니다.
국수주의.x: Excessive ultranationalism leads people to reject other cultures.
국수주의.e: Literally 'ism of the nation's pure essence' — nothing to do with 국수 'noodles'.
국수주의.t: 주의 is usually pronounced [주이] in everyday speech.

식도.x: I think some food is stuck in my esophagus.

막.x: This play consists of three acts in total.
막.e: Literally 'curtain': each act ends as the curtain falls.
막.t: 막을 내리다 (to lower the curtain) also means any event comes to an end.

민주화운동.x: In May 1980, a large pro-democracy movement broke out in Gwangju.
민주화운동.e: Literally 'movement to make the people the masters'.

상례.x: Traditional funeral rites had very complicated procedures.
상례.t: Pronounced [상녜] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

궁구하다.m: to study thoroughly, to investigate deeply
궁구하다.x: He spent his whole life deeply studying human nature.
궁구하다.e: Literally 'exhaust and investigate' — studying until nothing is left.

명철하다.ex: 그는 명철한 판단으로 회사를 위기에서 구했어요.
명철하다.x: He saved the company from crisis with his wise judgment.

석간.ex: 요즘은 석간을 발행하는 신문사가 많지 않아요.
석간.x: These days, not many newspaper companies publish an evening paper.

통찰하다.m: to see into, to gain insight into
통찰하다.ex: 그는 사회 문제의 본질을 정확히 통찰했습니다.
통찰하다.x: He accurately saw into the essence of the social problem.
통찰하다.e: Literally 'see through and examine' — grasping the core of something.

감미롭다.ex: 그 가수의 감미로운 목소리에 완전히 빠졌어요.
감미롭다.x: I completely fell for that singer's sweet, mellow voice.
감미롭다.e: Literally 'sweet and beautiful'; -롭다 turns it into an adjective.
감미롭다.t: Used for music, voices and moods; for food, say 달콤하다 or 달다 instead.

진면목.m: true face, true character, real worth
진면목.ex: 그는 위기 상황에서 진면목을 보여 주었어요.
진면목.x: He showed his true character in a crisis.

장삼이사.m: ordinary people, any Tom, Dick, or Harry
장삼이사.ex: 그런 일은 장삼이사 누구나 할 수 있어요.
장삼이사.x: Any ordinary person could do something like that.
장삼이사.e: Literally 'Zhang's third son and Lee's fourth son' — just anybody.

혹세무민.ex: 그 사이비 종교는 혹세무민으로 많은 사람을 속였습니다.
혹세무민.x: That cult deceived many people by misleading the public.
혹세무민.e: Literally 'deluding the world and deceiving the people.'
